title: The Mellow Eve Is Gliding
description: The Mellow Eve Is Gliding in Tonic Solfa to ST. ALPHEGE, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 944 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Reflections at Sunset”, where the book credits them to the Sacred Songs.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sevens and Sixes (7.6.7.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. ALPHEGE; any other Sevens and Sixes tune fits them as well.
underlay: The mel-low eve is glid-ing Se-rene-ly down the west; So, ev-ery care sub-sid-ing, My soul would sink to rest.

lines: My soul would sink to rest.
O, on the last bright morning

licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1853.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to ST. ALPHEGE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
